lead: Most of a page is text and data. HTML has a small set of elements for that job: headings, inline emphasis, links, lists, tables and images. Each element carries meaning, not just appearance. A screen reader can tell a table header from a cell, and a browser can follow a link or load an image. The same elements carry prices on a shopping page, marks in a result table, and captions under a photo. Learn the tags and their attributes once, and most static pages become easy to write by hand.
prereq: You need: Chapter 2.1 for elements, attributes and correct nesting.

blocks.text: Headings h1 to h6 rank content. h1 is the page main title; h6 is the lowest level. Use them in order. Do not pick a heading by its size; CSS sets size, as Chapter 2.7 shows.

Inline elements change meaning or display inside a line. b makes bold text with no extra importance. strong marks important text and usually looks bold. i sets italic text in an alternate voice. em marks stressed text and usually looks italic. u underlines. mark highlights like a pen. small is for side comments. sub makes subscript, as in H2O. sup makes superscript, as in x2.

code marks a code fragment. pre keeps spaces and line breaks, so it suits a code block or aligned text. br breaks a line inside a paragraph. hr marks a thematic break between sections. Use br and hr for meaning, not for spacing; margins from CSS (Chapter 2.6) do spacing.

A link is an a element with an href attribute. The value is a URL. An absolute URL has scheme and host, such as https://example.com/page. A relative URL is resolved against the current page, such as contact.html or ../images/logo.png. Use absolute URLs for other sites and relative URLs inside your own site.

target=_blank opens the link in a new tab; add rel=noopener with it. A mailto: URL starts a mail app, for example mailto:office@example.com. A tel: URL starts the phone dialler on a mobile. A jump link points to an element with an id: give a heading id=fees and link with href=#fees. An image can sit inside a link, so the picture becomes clickable. For example, <a href=page.html><img src=logo.png alt=Home></a>.

Lists group related items. ul is an unordered bullet list. ol is an ordered list; start=3 begins at 3, and type=A uses A, B, C. The allowed type values are 1, A, a, I and i. dl is a description list with dt for a term and dd for its description. For a nested list, put the inner ul or ol inside an li, never directly inside the outer list.

A table holds data in rows and columns. table contains an optional caption, then thead, tbody and tfoot. Each row is tr. A header cell is th; a data cell is td. Put scope=col on a column header and scope=row on a row header. Screen readers then connect each cell to its headers.

colspan=2 makes one cell cover two columns to its right. rowspan=2 makes it cover two rows downward. Count the cells in each row after merges. Never use a table for page layout; CSS layout is in Chapter 2.8. Old presentational attributes such as align and bgcolor are not the modern way; CSS borders, backgrounds and text alignment replaced them (Chapters 2.6 and 2.7).

An image uses img with src, the URL of the file. The alt attribute is required: it describes the image when the file is missing and for a screen reader. width and height are pixel sizes; they reserve space and reduce layout shift. loading=lazy delays loading an off-screen image. Wrap a picture and its caption in figure, with the caption in figcaption.

figure.caption: The footer row has only two td tags: Sum carries colspan=2 and so covers columns 1 and 2, while 70 sits in column 3. Check the body amounts: 20 + 50 = 70.

spec.title: Stationery bill grid
spec.aria: A grid of four rows and three columns: the header row is Item, Qty, Rs; the body rows are Pen 2 20 and Ink 1 50; in the footer row the first cell Sum is marked colspan=2 so it covers columns 1 and 2 of the three-column grid, and 70 is the cell in column 3.

examples.question: Write HTML5 markup for a price table. The header row is Item, Qty, Rs. The body rows are Pen 2 20 and Ink 1 50. The footer row has one cell reading Sum with colspan=2, then a last cell reading 70. Show the grid and check the arithmetic. Treat Rs as the line amount, not the unit price.
steps: Open table and add captionStationery bill/caption. In thead, make one tr with three th cells: Item, Qty, Rs. Give each scope=col.
In tfoot, the row has two td cells. The first is td colspan=2Sum; it covers columns 1 and 2. The second is td70 in column 3.
Grid check: rows 1 to 3 each use 3 cells. Row 4 uses 2 cells, but the first spans 2 columns, so row 4 still covers 3 columns. Total table size is 4 rows by 3 columns.
Amount check: Rs values are 20 and 50. Sum = 20 + 50 = 70. The quantities 2 and 1 are already reflected in the line amounts, so we do not multiply again.
examples.answer: The footer's first cell spans two columns; the total is Rs 70.
examples.check:
pen_rs = 20
ink_rs = 50
total_rs = pen_rs + ink_rs
print(total_rs)

traps: Swapping colspan (merge across columns) with rowspan (merge down rows). Count cells after each merge.
Using old align or bgcolor on table cells. These are presentational attributes; CSS handles alignment and background.
Writing img without alt. The text is required for accessibility and appears if the image fails to load.
Putting a nested ul directly inside another ul. It must go inside an li.
Treating b and strong as identical in meaning. Both usually look bold, but only strong says the text is important.

quiz.q: Which attribute holds the destination of an a link?

quiz.a: ul shows bullets with no order; ol shows a sequence with numbers or letters.

quiz.q: Write the opening tag for an ordered list that starts at 3.
quiz.a: <ol start=3>; the first item is numbered 3.

quiz.q: A table footer row has a first cell with colspan=2 and a second cell with 70. How many td tags are in that row, and which columns do they cover?
quiz.a: Two td tags. The first covers columns 1 and 2; the second covers column 3.

quiz.q: Why is a table a poor choice for placing a page sidebar and main text?
quiz.a: A table means row and column data. Layout tables confuse screen readers and break badly on small screens. CSS layout places boxes without false table semantics.

quiz.q: Why is alt required on an image?
quiz.a: It gives text when the image fails and a description for screen-reader users; it also helps search engines understand the image.

beyond: Not for the exam. Real pages add responsive images with srcset and picture, so a phone downloads a smaller file. Modern accessibility tools read the table header and scope relationships you write. Search for the HTML Living Standard table model, the loading=lazy attribute, and the srcset attribute. These are small extensions of the same tags.
